extracted.intended_audience: researchers, authors, editors, and scholarly publishers (stakeholders in research assessment and journal policy)
extracted.subtask_description: Publisher-level commitments and operational practices to implement the Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA) principles for assessing research and journal outputs. Describes actions Sage has taken (platform features, policy choices, and metrics presentation) to align publishing practices with DORA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce constraints on the number of references allowable in research articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage allows editors and their editorial boards to determine the number of references allowed per manuscript. We are committed to sharing the aims of DORA with these stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy: editorial boards, not hard publisher limits, should set reference limits. Rationale: reducing artificial constraints supports appropriate citation practice and fuller crediting of prior work. (No numerical limits specified; emphasis is on editorial discretion and DORA communication.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove access restrictions or reuse limitations on an article's reference list
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage is a participating publisher in the Initiative for Open Citations (I4OC), and all articles are published with freely available reference lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions: publish reference lists as openly available (I4OC participation); provide article sharing functionality (Sage Journals article sharing tool) that allows authors to share a read-only article version so colleagues can view articles without a subscription. Rationale: facilitate reuse, indexing, and transparent citation data to support assessment beyond closed metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage responsible authorship practices, including details on the contributions of each author
rubrics_metrics.description: Over time, Sage will be adding Contributor Roles Taxonomy (CRediT) on the majority of our journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation: journals should capture and display author contribution information (CRediT taxonomy) to make authorship responsibilities transparent. Practical note: Sage links to a CRediT page on their Author Gateway for more information and is progressively rolling this out across journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make article-level metrics available to encourage assessment based on the content of the article rather than a journal’s publication metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors and readers can see article metrics for every article we publish, including article usage and citations from Crossref and Web of Science. Each journal homepage features top downloaded articles, top-cited articles, and articles trending on Altmetric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation: expose article-level usage and citation counts and display attention indicators (e.g., Altmetric) on article pages and journal homepages. Purpose: enable assessment of individual article impact rather than relying solely on journal-level proxies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce emphasis on Impact Factor as a promotional tool and present a variety of metrics for researchers to use to assess a journal’s performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Our comprehensive journal metrics pages cover metrics from Journal Citation Reports, Scopus, and Google Scholar, as well as full-text usage and abstract and indexing services, among others. With regard to citation-based impact metrics, we place emphasis on the five-year Journal Impact Factors (JIF) alongside the standard two-year measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practices & examples: provide broad journal metrics pages combining multiple sources; emphasize five-year JIF to provide a longer-term picture; offer tools (Sage Policy Profiles powered by Overton) to discover policy citations; run initiatives such as a '10-Year Impact Award' to recognize long-term impact beyond immediate citations; supply explanatory resources (Understanding Journal Metrics information website, white papers, interviews, thought pieces) to help researchers use metrics responsibly.
